flaws.Impatient: Take a -2 penalty to checks involving patience and may act impulsively in tense situations.
flaws.Overconfidence: Take a -2 penalty to checks involving risk assessment and may push yourself too hard.
flaws.Arrogant: Take a -2 penalty to Persuade checks and have difficulty acknowledging others’ opinions.
flaws.Addiction: Your character is addicted to a substance or habit. Take a -2 penalty to all checks when unable to satisfy this addiction, but a +1 to all checks for 1d4 hours after satisfying the addiction.
flaws.Loner: Take a -2 penalty to teamwork-related checks and struggle to work effectively in groups.
flaws.Greedy: Take a -2 penalty to MND saves to resist the lure of wealth or power, and may take reckless and selfish actions in pursuit of wealth or power.
flaws.Mistrustful: Take a -2 penalty to Persuade checks and have difficulty trusting others, leading to strained relationships.
flaws.Vengeful: Take a -2 penalty to MND saving throws against letting go of grudges, which may lead to reckless decisions.
flaws.Envious: Take a -2 penalty to MND checks when interacting with those who have something your character desires.
flaws.Pacifist: Take a -2 penalty to attack rolls and struggle to engage in combat, preferring peaceful resolutions.

aspects.Lowlight Vision: Halflings are used to spending nights under the stars and walking through shadows and thus have lowlight vision. They’ve developed this over years of being in dark lands, living in forests and being active at night under the light of the moon and stars. +1 Trait: Due to Halflings being less focused on active training, they tend to pick up traits a little easier, it comes naturally to them. Cultural Traits
aspects.Dark Vision: Gnomes have the trait Dark Vision, this is the ability to see in complete darkness as if it were daylight for up to 60 ft. They’ve developed this over years of living underground and being active in cave systems totally devoid of light. +1 Trait: Due to Gnomes being less focused on active training, they tend to pick up traits a little easier, it comes naturally to them.
aspects.Scale Armor: Many Scaled inherit their lizard parent’s hardened scales; Some covering their entire bodies or having patches here and there. No matter the coverage, Scaled gain +2 Natural DR, which stacks with any armor they wear and they gain Resistance to elemental damage from Fire and Ice.
aspects.Compound Vision: Due to the formation of the Arrasect’s eyes, Arresects are hard to sneak up on and are not considered flanked when approached from either side. They gain a +2 to all Detect checks.
aspects.Winged Flight: Av'riahls can fly at a speed equal to DEX x3 (rounded to the nearest 5) and can sustain flight for up to 10 hours. After flying, they must rest their wings for 1 hour per hour flown before flying again. * In combat: Av’riahls must make a BOD saving throw every ½ their BOD score (rounded down) rounds to stay airborne. The DC is 10 + the number of rounds flown and increases with each interval. If they fail this save (for any reason other than being struck), they gain exhaustion and fall, taking fall damage. When hit while flying, they must make a BOD save (DC 10 + damage taken) or fall, but this does not cause exhaustion. * In Long-Distance Travel: Av'riahls must make a BOD save each hour of flight, starting at DC 20 + 1 per hour flown. Failure forces them to land, gain exhaustion, and rest. * Av'riahls can glide to avoid fall damage unless they are exhausted.
aspects.Natural Weapons: Zizses’ claws, teeth, and tail serve as powerful natural weapons. Their claws deal 1d6 damage in unarmed combat as long as they’re not covered. Their sharp teeth and strong bite deal 2d4 damage, while their tail can be used as a bludgeoning weapon, dealing 1d6 damage. The specific natural weapons a Zizs has are determined by their unique reptilian features.
aspects.Terrán Physiology: Terrán are deeply connected to sunlight and nature, allowing them to thrive without traditional sustenance. They do not need to eat, as sunlight sustains them, and while in direct sunlight and out of combat, they can restore HP equal to ¼ of their BOD score per hour by absorbing water. Additionally, Terrán can regrow severed limbs as part of their natural healing process. If a body part is lost, the Terrán’s max HP is temporarily reduced by an amount proportional to the missing part (for example, losing a hand reduces max HP by roughly 1/10, a whole arm by 1/5, or both legs by 2/5). Once the Terrán heals to their full HP, they continue healing at half speed until their max HP is fully restored, at which point the missing part regrows. Terrán take double damage from elemental damage. As a FRA, Terrán can disguise themselves as a plant of their size and shape. Identifying them requires a successful Detect check (DC 20) and a Knowledge (Nature) check (DC 25). Cultural Traits
aspects.Fungal Physiology: Shroomites are immune to bleed effects and bone breaks, and decapitation does not kill them. They can regrow missing body parts as part of their natural healing process. If a body part is lost, the Shroomite’s max HP is temporarily reduced by an amount proportional to the missing part (for example, losing a hand reduces max HP by roughly 1/10, a whole arm by 1/5, or both legs by 2/5). Once the Shroomite heals to their full HP, they continue healing at half speed until their max HP is fully restored, at which point the missing part regrows. Shroomites take double damage from elemental sources. Additionally, as a FRA, they can transform into a fungal shape, appearing either as a patch of mushrooms or as a single large mushroom. Identifying them requires a successful Detect check (DC 20) and a Knowledge (Nature) check (DC 25). Shroomites are immune to the ill effects of consuming rotting food and in fact find it to be nutritious. Cultural Traits
aspects.Mana Keen Construct: Manakeens are immune to hunger, thirst, exhaustion, fear, and non-magical poisons or diseases. They cannot heal through rest or herbal potions but begin with a mana pool of 5 plus their MND score. If they gain a casting feat, they instead use the casting feat’s manapool and add 5. Manakeens can expend 1 Mana to boost a check by +1, enhance damage by +1 (treated as magical for DR), or heal for 1d4 HP. During rest, they heal HP equal to four times their remaining mana and regain mana at a rate of ¼ BOD per hour.
